title: Restore root loses the active Field presentation
impact: A Field user is shown neutral white text and spinner during restore instead of the red/black night-vision presentation.
recommendation: Carry the effective Field theme/filter into the standalone restoring app without touching backup/data semantics. Inspect unsupported-database roots separately; their unknown persisted theme is not waived by this audit.

title: Four record headers still force a single line
impact: At 200%, complete record identity is visually cut to Andromed / DSLR 135 / Kyiv although the title widget contains the full name. Session dates disappear. The app bar can reserve wrapping height while the child forbids wrapping.
recommendation: Remove caller-imposed line clamps and verify complete names/date at 375 dp, with the shared app-bar measurement corrected.

title: Shared AppBar estimates 48 dp actions although the actual Field action is 64 dp at 200%
impact: Appearance is laid out as two lines in a 64 dp toolbar, with a text rectangle at y=-23, height 110: the title is cut off at the top. The helper measured a wider title slot than Material actually provides.
recommendation: Measure the actual available leading/title/action constraints at the user scale, retaining full names and reachable 48 dp controls. Do not reduce text size to hide the defect.

title: Record facts keep two narrow columns at 200%
impact: FactRows shares width between Flexible label/value columns. Manufacturer breaks inside the word, units and coordinates require excessive lines, and scanning a fact pair becomes slow. There is no RenderFlex exception to catch this.
recommendation: Stack each label/value/note pair when its measured width or text scale requires it; retain units, full names and tabular values.

title: Fill the window touches the preceding capture action
impact: Build calibration and Fill the window share a boundary with zero gap. At 200%, calibration y=266 h=96 ends exactly where Fill y=362 begins; both are 303 dp wide, so the controls read as a joined box.
recommendation: Add the existing 8 dp inter-action separation at the composition boundary; keep both actions and their large-text stacking.

title: Record result footer buttons have unequal height at 200%
impact: Cancel is 161.5 x 56 dp at y=724; Save result is 161.5 x 112 dp at y=696. The center-aligned Row makes the pair visibly uneven when Save result wraps. Other editors already use LibrarySaveBar with equal-height stretching.
recommendation: Use the established equal-height footer anatomy, preserve form validation/Save/Cancel, and verify with IME insets and both scales.

title: Library child lists, records and editors retain the former composition
impact: The Library index has the new grouped surface, but the next tap returns to bare list/record/form sections. Camera/Optics, position/name/zone and catalogue/own targets are separated only by whitespace or rules.
recommendation: Specify coherent groups per child screen: record identity/actions, measured facts, optional detail; editor field groups and search/result sections. Preserve manage-versus-select semantics, lazy lists and the accepted current-site/saved-sites/alternative-position order.

title: Plan choosers, capture/assumption/calibration editors and candidate list remain outside the grouping direction
impact: Opening an action from grouped Plan changes to a long ungrouped form or list. Site/night, exposure/count/recording, timing/storage overrides and calibration frame types have distinct reading tasks that are currently differentiated mainly by spacing.
recommendation: Define groups around existing tasks, preserving Apply-to-draft versus explicit Save plan, choice/search semantics, conditional fields, scientific warnings and input widths at 200%. Candidate filters and results should stay lazy/scrollable.

title: Logbook entry details and Progress retain the old flat document
impact: The month-grouped Logbook index opens records whose outcome/actions, planned-versus-recorded values, saved snapshot, notes and export have no corresponding surface groups. Progress similarly mixes target, filter and rig subtotals in one long page.
recommendation: Group existing reading tasks while preserving planned/recorded separation, immutable snapshots, comparable-group rules and export/delete ownership. Avoid one card per data row.

title: Settings child pages retain old whitespace/rule sectioning
impact: The grouped Preferences/Data index opens ungrouped Theme/Text/Units/Weather, planning defaults, privacy, backup and About documents. The parent/child visual language is inconsistent, especially in long editor pages.
recommendation: Group related existing settings, separate backup from restore and informational notices, retain immediate-versus-staged changes, persistence feedback and current Save/Cancel ownership.
